newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stock funds seen aiding share prices.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stock funds seen aiding share prices.

text.p: Stocks that are attractive to the local pension fund system have the biggest upside potential on the Argentine bolsa, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell chief economist Raul Buonoume said Thursday.

"In addition to company fundamentals, DMG believes that two issues should be considered: the potential for AFJP's (private pension funds) to increase their stake and the average daily traded volume. A stock that is easily traded and that pension funds can continue to buy has greater potential than its peers," Buonoume said in an investors' report.
On this basis he recommended purchases of holding company Perez Companc, oil giant YPF, Banco Frances, Siderca, Molinos, Transportadora de Gas del Sur and Siderar.
DMG noted that AFJPs coffers are swelling and reached $4.48 billion in September, an increase of over 135 percent in 12 months.

"We conservatively estimate that the pension funds could have $5.17 billion under management by the end of the year, which should increase to $7.97 billion by the end of 1997 and $19 billion by the end of the year 2000," said Buonoume.

Although the percentage of funds invested in equities is just under 15 percent of total funds, this share is rapidly growing, said DMG. Between December 1995 and September 1996, the AFJPs more than doubled their stake in equities from 5.9 percent to 14.8 percent.

"There is still lots of room for growth; the regulatory body has authorized that a maximum of 35 percent of total funds can be invested in equities. Furthermore we estimate that 35 percent of all new funds received this year will flow into equities," said Buonoume.
